INTRODUCTION OF PRIME MINISTER, THE LEADER OF THE 
HOUSE AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, I have great pleasure in 
introducing the hon. Prime Minister of India, Dr. Manmohan Singh. 
I have also to inform that I had received a letter dated the 1 st 
June,2004 from Shri Ghulam Nabi A zad, the Minister of Parliamentary 
Affairs and the Minister of Urban Development; informing me that Dr. 
Manmohan Singh, the Prime Minister of India will the Leader of the 
House in Rajya Sabha. 
I have to inform Members that I have recognised Shri Jaswant 
Singh, Leader of the Bharatiya Janata Party in Rajya Sabha, as the Leader 
of the Opposition in Rajya Sabha with effect from 3rd June, 2004. 
ANNOUNCEMENT REGARDING RESIGNATION OF AN HON. 
MEMBER 
MR. CHAIRMAN: I have to inform Members that I had 
received a letter from Shri Man Mohan Samal, a Member representing the 
State of Orissa resigning his seat in  the Rajya Sabha. I have accepted his 
resignation with effect from the 23rd May, 2004.

OBITUARY REFERENCES 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, I refer with profound sorrow to 
the passing away of Shri Sikander Bakht and Shri S.B. Chavan, former 
Members and Sardar Gurcharan Singh Tohra and Dr. Abrar Ahmed, sitting 
Members and Dr. Shrikant Ramchandra Jichkar, a former Member of this 
House. 
Shri Sikander Bakht passed away on the 23rd February, 2004, at 
the age of 86 years. Born at Delhi in August, 1918, Shri Bakht had his 
education at Anglo-Arabic College, Delhi and Delhi University. A political 
and social worker, Shri Bakht took keen interest in sports, Indian classical 
music and Urdu poetry. Shri Bakht was also associated with various social 
welfare and educational institutions. He  was also Chairman of the Delhi 
Electricity Supply Undertaking. He was conferred the Padma Vibhushan 
Award in the year 2000. 
Shri Bakht started his political career with the membership of 
Municipal Corporation of Delhi and Delhi Metropolitan Council. He was 
Member of the Sixth Lok Sabha from 1977 to 1979. Shri Bakht 
represented the State of Madhy a Pradesh in this House for two 
consecutive terms from April, 1990 to April, 1996 and again from April, 
1996 
to April, 2002. Shri Bakht had the dis tinction to serve as the Leader of the 
Opposition in Rajya Sabha and also as  the Leader of the House in Rajya 
Sabha. He was the Leader of the O pposition in Rajya Sabha from July, 
1992 to May, 1996 and again from June, 1996 to March, 1998 and the 
Leader of the House in Rajya Sabha from March, 1998 to November, 1999. 
He was Chairman of the Department -related Parliamentary Standing 
Committee on Commerce from December,  1999 till April, 2002 and was 
also Chairman of the Joint Parlia mentary Committee on the functioning of 
Wakf Boards from October, 1996 to  December, 1997 and again from May, 
2000 to April, 2002. 
Shri Bakht served as Union Minist er for several years and held the 
portfolios of Works Housing, Supply, Rehabilitation and Wakf, Urban 
Affairs 
and Employment, External Affairs and Industry. He was Vice-President of 
the Bharatiya Janata Party from 1982 to 1993. Shri Bakht was known for 
his humility and simplicity. He enriched the debates of this House by his 
valuable contributions. A widely travelled person, Shri Bakht was member 
of various Indian Parliamentary delegations and represented the country in 
several International events.  He attended the Inter-Parliamentary Union

ShriBakht was the Governor of Ke rala from April, 2002 till he 
breathed his last.In the passing away of Shri Sikander Bakht, the country has 
lost an eminent Parliamentarian and an able administrator. 
Shri S.B. Chavan passed away on the 26th February 2004, at the 
age of 84 years, after a prolonged illness. Born at Paithan, District 
Aurangabad, Maharashtra in July 1920, Shri Chavan had his education at 
Madras University and Osmania University. An advocate by profession,  
ShriChavan participated in the freedom struggle in former Hyderabad 
State right from his student days and gave up practice during the Quit Court 
Movement there. He was also associated  with various social and educational 
organisations. He was Chancellor of the Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth, a 
deemed University, in Pune and wa s President of the  anded Town 
Municipality and Bharat Scouts and Guides, New Delhi. He also served as 
Chairman of the Indian Institute of Public Administration, New Delhi. 
Shri Chavan had a long and distinguished political career starting 
with membership of the Bombay State Legislative Council in 1956. In 1957 
he was elected to the Maharashtra Le gislative Assembly and remained a 
Member of that Assembly till 1980. He was elected to the Maharashtra 
Legislative Council in 1986 and remain ed a Member of it till 1988. Shri 
Chavan held the Office of the Chief Mi nister of Maharashtra twice, from 
1975 to 1977 and again from March 1986 to June 1988. Shri Chavan was 
also a Member of the Seventh and the Eighth Lok Sabha. He represented 
the State of Maharashtra in this House for three terms, from October 1988 
to April 1990, April 1990 to April 1996 and again from April 1996 to April 
2002. Shri Chavan was th e Leader of the House in Rajya Sabha from July, 
1991 to May, 1996. He also acted as the Leader of the Opposition in 
Rajya Sabha from 23rd to 31st May 1996. He was Chairman of the 
Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Human Resource 
Development from 1996 to 2002 and was also Chairman of the Ethics 
Committee from 1997 to 2002. 
Shri Chavan served as Union Minister for several years and held

defence, Home Affairs and Finance. He also had the distinction of serving 
as the Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission of India from 
August1981 to July 1984. 
In the passing away of Shri S.B. Chavan, the country has lost an 
outstanding Parliamentarian, an eminent political personality and an able 
administrator who made valuable contributions in diverse sectors of 
national life. 
Sardar Gurcharan Singh Tohra passed away on the 1st April 2004, 
at the age of 80 years. Bom at Village  Tohra, District Patiala, Punjab, in 
September, 1924, Sardar Tohra had his education at Gurumukhi vldyalaya, 
Patiaia and Punjab University, Lahore. An agriculturist and a social worker, 
Sardar Gurcharan Singh Tohra was associated with various social, 
educational and religious organisations. He took keen interest in the welfare 
and uplift of weaker sections of the so ciety and in the religious affairs. He 
was Vice-President of the Shiromani Akali Dal from 1958 to i960 and again 
from 1962 to 1965. Sardar Tohra was President of  the Shiromani 
Gurudwara Prabandhak Committee from 1973 to 1999, with only a short 
break of about one year in betwee n. Sardar Tohra was also founder 
President of the Sarb Hind Shiromani Akali Dal and Chairman of the Sikh 
Education Society, Chandigarh, Gu ru Nanak Khalsa College, Mumbai, 
Nankana Sahib Education Trust and Guru Ram Das Charitable Trust. He 
was imprisoned a number of times during his life time for espousing 
different causes including that of farmers and protection of Human Rights. 
Sardar Tohra represented the State of Punjab in this House from 
March, 1969 to April, 1970; April, 1970 to April, 1976; May, 1980 to April, 
1982; April, 1982 to April, 1988 and again from April, 1998 till he breathed 
his last. He was also elected to Rajya Sabha in the recently held biennial 
election from the State of Punjab and his fresh term of office was to 
commence from the 10th Apr il, 2004. Sardar Tohra was also a Member of 
the Sixth Lok Sabha. A deeply religio us person, Shri Tohra remained a 
simple man and was always accessible to people from all walks of life. 
In the passing away of Sardar Gurcharan Singh Tohra, the country 
has lost an eminent religious personality and a veteran Parliamentarian.

Dr. Shrikant Ramchandra Jichkar passed away on the 2nd -June,

REFERENCE TO VICTIMS OF IED BLAST IN JAMMU AND 
KASHMIR 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, it is with utmost grief and sorrow 
that I refer to the tragic killing of twenty-nine persons, comprising twelve 
BSF personnel and seventeen of their relatives and family members, and 
injury of five others in the blast that occurred near the Lower Munda, 
Anantnag, on the Jammu-Srinagar National Highway in Jammu and 
Kashmir on the 23rd May, 2004. No words are strong enough to condemn 
this gruesome act. The killing of so many innooent people has shocked the 
entire nation. I am sure that the wh ole House will join me in condemning 
this cowardly and senseless act an d in offering condolences to the 
bereaved families and expressing concern and sympathy for those who got 
injured. 
(Hon. Members then stood in silence for one minute)
